what: The "Derived geometry (host, from the padded shape)" table gives folded_H = prod(padded_shape[:-1]) and W = padded_shape[-1] without saying WHICH tensor s padded shape. For a ROW_MAJOR-sharded input the two differ: the input rounds its last dim up to a whole number of shard widths (logical W=160 with shard_W=96 is stored as padded W=192) while the TILE output keeps the logical width. Worse, the justification right below ("The fold is exact because ... H %% 32 == 0 guarantees no leading dim straddles a tile boundary") only holds for the LOGICAL shape, so it actively reinforces the wrong reading. Deriving Wt from the input inflated it and corrupted every writer page index: 26 reference-grader cells failed with whole-tensor mismatch (Max ATOL 0.996) plus OOM where the inflated split oversized the plan.
suggest: State explicitly that the tile grid comes from the OUTPUT tensor padded shape, and that the INPUT padded last dim is a source row stride only (row_page_stride = in_padded_row_bytes / in_page_bytes). Add a line to the Risks table: "a ROW_MAJOR-sharded input pads its last dim to a multiple of shard_W; the TILE output does not - never take W from the input".

what: Layer A1 says "Profiler is on by default in ./build_metal.sh" and only documents the out-of-process route (python -m tracy + ops_perf_results CSV). It never mentions that the IN-PROCESS route every in-tree example actually uses - ttnn.ReadDeviceProfiler + ttnn.get_latest_programs_perf_data - silently returns an EMPTY DICT unless TT_METAL_DEVICE_PROFILER=1, TT_METAL_PROFILER_MID_RUN_DUMP=1 and TT_METAL_PROFILER_CPP_POST_PROCESS=1 are ALL set before the device opens. Second undocumented gotcha: ReadDeviceProfiler after a SINGLE launch reliably returns an empty window, so per-launch reads yield nothing and reads must be batched per round. Cost two failed bench runs and a probe before I found the requirement buried in the nanobind docstring at ttnn/cpp/ttnn-nanobind/profiler.cpp:174.
suggest: Add an A0/A1b subsection for the in-process measurement recipe: the three required env vars (set before device open), the flush-read/N-launches/work-read bracketing, and a pointer to tests/ttnn/unit_tests/operations/examples/test_double_buffer.py:20-27 + 78-105 as the canonical copyable harness.
